title: pastinaca heracleoides
intro: Pastinaca heracleoides, commonly known as wild parsnip, is a biennial plant in the carrot family (Apiaceae). It is native to Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa, and has been naturalized in many parts of the world. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, which have been attributed to its ability to reduce fever, soothe skin irritations, and aid in digestion. The bioactive constituents of Pastinaca heracleoides include alkaloids, glycosides, and essential oils, which exhibit therapeutic actions such as analgesic, antispasmodic, and diuretic effects.
